chart.title: Present progressive for future plans
chart.note_rule: Form: am / is / are + verb-ing. Use for scheduled future events.
chart.note_exception: Common time expressions: tomorrow, next week, tonight, on [day]

tab1_samples.text: I'm meeting my cousins after school today.
tab1_samples.jp: 今日放課後、いとこたちに会います。

tab1_samples.text: She's visiting Tokyo for the first time next spring.
tab1_samples.jp: 彼女は来春、初めて東京を訪れます。
今夜、家族で夕食を食べます。
彼は木曜日にロンドンへ飛びます。

tab1_samples.text: They're coming to our house this Sunday.
tab1_samples.jp: 彼らはこの日曜日に私たちの家に来ます。

tab1_samples.text: I'm not going to school tomorrow — it's a public holiday.
tab1_samples.jp: 明日は祝日なので学校に行きません。

tab1_samples.text: Are you visiting your relatives next summer?
tab1_samples.jp: 来年の夏、親戚を訪ねる予定ですか？

tab1_samples.text: My parents are planning a big birthday party for me.
tab1_samples.jp: 両親が私のために大きな誕生日パーティーを計画しています。

tab1_samples.text: Leo is studying with his friends this afternoon.
tab1_samples.jp: レオは今日の午後、友達と勉強します。

tab1_samples.text: We're watching the big game together on Saturday night.
tab1_samples.jp: 土曜日の夜、みんなで大試合を観ます。

rules.title: Form — am / is / are + verb-ing
rules.subtitle: Choose the correct form of be, then add -ing to the verb.

examples.text: I am meeting my friend at 3 pm.
examples.jp: 午後3時に友達に会います。

examples.text: She is visiting her aunt next weekend.
examples.jp: 彼女は来週末、おばさんを訪ねます。

rules.title: Use for scheduled future events
rules.subtitle: Only when you already have a plan or schedule — not for habits or general facts.

examples.text: I'm seeing the doctor on Monday. (scheduled appointment)
examples.jp: 月曜日に医者に行きます（予約済みの診察）。

examples.text: She's starting her new school next term. (definite plan)
examples.jp: 彼女は来学期から新しい学校に通い始めます（確定した予定）。

rules.title: Common future time expressions
rules.subtitle: These words and phrases signal a future plan — look for them as clues.

examples.jp: 彼らは明日到着します。
来月、引っ越しをします。

rules.title: Negative — am / is / are + not + verb-ing
rules.subtitle: To say something is not happening, add not after the helping verb.

transforms.to: I am not going (I'm not going)
she is not coming (she isn't coming)
they are not staying (they aren't staying)

examples.jp: パーティーには行きません。
彼女は来ません——仕事があります。

rules.title: Questions — Am / Is / Are + subject + verb-ing?
rules.subtitle: Move the helping verb to the front to make a question.

examples.jp: パーティーに来ますか？
レオは私たちと一緒に飛行機に乗りますか？

mixed_samples.text: My teacher is testing us on Friday, so I'm studying tonight.
mixed_samples.jp: 先生が金曜日にテストをするので、今夜勉強しています。

mixed_samples.text: She isn't coming to practice — she has a doctor's appointment.
mixed_samples.jp: 彼女は練習に来ません——医者の予約があります。

mixed_samples.text: Are they arriving by train or by bus?
mixed_samples.jp: 彼らは電車で来ますか、それともバスで来ますか？

mixed_samples.text: We're having a big family meal tomorrow evening.
mixed_samples.jp: 明日の夕方、家族で大きな食事をします。

mixed_samples.text: I'm not watching TV tonight — I have homework.
mixed_samples.jp: 今夜はテレビを見ません——宿題があります。
彼は来週月曜日から新しい仕事を始めます。
パーティーに何か持ってきますか？

mixed_samples.text: My parents are flying to New York on the 15th.
mixed_samples.jp: 両親は15日にニューヨークへ飛行機で行きます。

mixed_samples.text: She isn't visiting us this weekend — the weather is bad.
mixed_samples.jp: 天気が悪いので、彼女は今週末、私たちを訪ねません。

mixed_samples.text: We're meeting our old friends from primary school this Saturday.
mixed_samples.jp: この土曜日に小学校の旧友たちに会います。

explanation.title: Use be + verb-ing for future plans
explanation.body: "Next Sunday" signals a future plan. With "I", use am + verb-ing → am visiting. "Visit" alone is simple present (a habit), not a future plan.

explanation.title: She → is + verb-ing
explanation.body: With "she", always use is (not "are"). The verb-ing form is needed because this is a planned future event: is working. "Working" alone has no helping verb.

explanation.title: Questions: Are + they + verb-ing?
explanation.body: To ask a question with the present progressive, move the helping verb to the front. "They" uses are → Are they coming? "Do" is for simple present, not progressive.

explanation.title: Negative: be + not + verb-ing
explanation.body: After "is not", add the verb-ing form: going. The structure is: he is not + verb-ing. We never say "is not go" or "is not went".

explanation.title: We → are + verb-ing
explanation.body: "We" uses are. Dinner at 7 tonight is a scheduled plan → use present progressive: are having. "Have" is simple present; "is having" uses the wrong helping verb for "we".

explanation.title: I + am + verb-ing
explanation.body: "I" always uses am. "Tomorrow" signals a future plan → am leaving. "Leaving" alone has no helping verb; "left" is past tense.

explanation.title: She → is + verb-ing
explanation.body: "Next month" = future plan. "She" uses is → is visiting. "Are visiting" uses the wrong helping verb; "visited" is past tense.

explanation.title: They → are + verb-ing
explanation.body: "They" uses are. "On Friday" = scheduled departure → use present progressive: are flying. "Flies" is simple present 3rd person singular; "is flying" uses the wrong helping verb.

explanation.title: I + am + verb-ing
explanation.body: "This weekend" = future plan. "I" uses am → am meeting. "Meet" is simple present; "meeting" alone has no helping verb.

stem: with us — she has other plans.

explanation.title: Negative: isn't / aren't + verb-ing
explanation.body: "She" uses is → negative is isn't coming. "Aren't coming" uses the wrong helping verb; "not coming" has no helping verb; "doesn't coming" mixes forms incorrectly.

stem: dinner — it'll be ready in 20 minutes.
